raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Declare that Triton MLA can serve a non-causal multi-token decode block while the MLA KV cache is DCP-sharded, scoped to ROCm.

`forward_mqa` already flattens a non-causal block into one decode row per query token. Every row attends the same committed prefix, so a rank-local `seq_len` fully describes the row under DCP. Without this capability, backend selection rejects Triton MLA for this combination and pushes the multi-token block away from its decode path.

## Why this is separate

This is split out of #51705 on reviewer request. #51705 implements causal multi-token target verification in the ROCm AITER backend; this two-line capability is the only part that touches a backend shared with CUDA and XPU.

## Scope and behavior

`AttentionBackend.supports_non_causal_dcp()` is a backend-eligibility gate, and Triton MLA is selectable on CUDA, XPU, and ROCm. The flatten itself is platform independent, but this DCP configuration has only been validated on ROCm, so the capability remains `current_platform.is_rocm()`.

A single module-level constant feeds both read sites: the class capability and the `supports_dcp_with_varlen` builder argument. With DCP disabled, behavior is unchanged. With DCP enabled on ROCm, a non-causal multi-token group retains its decode reorder threshold instead of being forced back to single-token support. Only the affected KV-cache group is promoted to `UNIFORM_BATCH` graph support.

## Validation

Revision: `8474084088b12b7bc3ca35cf6d74f87cb7161f92`

```text
python3 -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_triton_mla_capabilities.py -v
3 passed, 14 warnings
```

The tests cover the ROCm-scoped capability, both read sites, the retained multi-token reorder threshold under DCP, and conditional graph-support promotion.

### Full-model stacked validation

This revision was cleanly stacked on #51705 at `e1843114b7c233a9c71ad44b28bf63426ad64836` and tested with real Kimi-K3 target and Kimi-K3-DSpark weights. Configuration: TP8/DCP8, A2A DCP, FP8 target KV, 1,048,576 maximum model length, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs through batch 32, two draft tokens, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling, and Triton MLA for the draft.

```text
combined focused tests:       543 passed, 14 warnings in 31.75s
GSM8K 5-shot:                 1319/1319 at concurrency 64
strict-match exact_match:     0.9628506444 +/- 0.0052095163
flexible-extract exact_match: 0.9636087945 +/- 0.0051581135
evaluation time:              353 seconds
mean acceptance length:       2.67-2.74 in the final 10 windows
server errors/tracebacks:     0/0
HSA memory-access faults:     0
```

The run selected Triton MLA for the non-causal draft and ROCm AITER MLA for the target, completed FULL graph capture, and remained healthy after evaluation.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and is responsible for defending it.

<!-- vllm-ci-command:5518387597 -->

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @YukioZzz.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Hi @YukioZzz, thanks for this. We need this PR merged to have  Kimi-K3 + DSpark + DCP working on gfx942 (MI325X): ROCM_AITER_MLA has no non-causal decode kernels there, so TRITON_MLA is the only backend that can serve the DSpark draft, and today that only works at DCP 1.

Would you have time to work on this? It needs a rebase, but the rebase isn't just a plain conflict fix. 

#51065 (merged Sep 18) removed the `_init_reorder_batch_threshold(...)` block in `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` that your second hunk edits. On main, the threshold is set once in `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__`, and `_init_reorder_batch_threshold` clamps it to 1 under DCP unless `supports_dcp_with_varlen` is passed. So keeping only the capability flag isn't enough. The draft passes backend selection and `_validate_dspark_dcp_support`, but its builder stays at threshold 1. FULL cudagraph capture of the 7-token draft block would then trip `assert m.max_query_len <= self.reorder_batch_threshold` in `build_for_cudagraph_capture` (from reading the code; we did not run the flag-only variant).

The obvious fix, passing `supports_dcp_with_varlen=True` from TRITON_MLA, is unsafe. It also raises the threshold for causal TRITON_MLA groups under DCP, such as an MTP/Eagle target. Their multi-token verify would then go to `forward_mqa` and hit `assert self.dcp_world_size == 1, "causal multi-token decode is not supported with DCP"`. Today those batches safely run as prefill.

We need this PR moving so **how would you like to proceed?** Any of these works for us:

1. You rebase this with the proper fix.
2. We open a follow-up PR with your two commits kept as authored by you, plus our fix on top with you as co-author, and close this one.
3. We push it to your branch, with your OK of course.

Please let us know what works best for you. Thanks in advance!

@xaguilar-amd Thanks for the detailed analysis! MI355x does not need this so I did not push this forward before. But now I have no bandwidth to test it, so option 2 works for me. You're welcome to cherry-pick my commits into a follow-up PR, add your fix, and run E2E validation. We can close this PR once the replacement is up. Thanks for taking this forward!
@YukioZzz alright! Sounds good! I'll let you know when the follow-up PR is up. Thanks!
@YukioZzz I opened a follow-up PR here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64261

@@ -39,6 +39,15 @@
 _MIN_WORK_PER_SPLIT = 512
 _SPLIT_OCCUPANCY_MULTIPLIER = 2
 
+# Triton MLA can serve a non-causal multi-token block while the MLA cache is
+# DCP-sharded: forward_mqa flattens the block to one decode row per query token
+# and every row sees the same committed prefix, so a rank-local seq_len is the
+# whole story. Only ROCm has been validated end to end (DSpark draft against a
+# DCP-sharded target), so the capability stays scoped to it until another
+# platform is measured. One constant keeps the backend eligibility gate and the
+# reorder threshold from disagreeing.
+_SUPPORTS_NONCAUSAL_MULTITOKEN_DCP = current_platform.is_rocm()
+
 
 def _compute_num_kv_splits(max_seq_len: int, sm_count: int) -> int:
     # Power of 2 to avoid excessive kernel instantiations, capped by an SM-based
@@ -56,6 +65,9 @@ class TritonMLAMetadataBuilder(MLACommonMetadataBuilder[MLACommonMetadata]):
     # Non-causal DSpark block is flattened to one decode row per query token in
     # forward_mqa, so no intra-block causal masking is required.
     supports_non_causal_multi_token_decode: ClassVar[bool] = True
+    supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp: ClassVar[bool] = (
+        _SUPPORTS_NONCAUSAL_MULTITOKEN_DCP
+    )
 
     @classmethod
     def get_cudagraph_support(
@@ -93,7 +105,11 @@ def __init__(self, kv_cache_spec, layer_names, vllm_config, device):
         # the decode path; raise its reorder threshold to the spec block length
         # so full-cudagraph capture admits it. Causal usage stays single-token.
         if getattr(self, "non_causal_multi_token_decode", False):
-            self._init_reorder_batch_threshold(1, supports_spec_as_decode=True)
+            self._init_reorder_batch_threshold(
+                1,
+                supports_spec_as_decode=True,
+                supports_dcp_with_varlen=_SUPPORTS_NONCAUSAL_MULTITOKEN_DCP,
+            )
         self._reserve_attn_logits_workspace()
 
     def update_draft_decode_metadata(self, _metadata: MLACommonMetadata) -> None:
